title: Last Stone Weight
kidExplanation: Story version: To simulate the process of smashing stones, we can use a max-heap (priority queue) to keep track of the stone weights. At each step, we pop the two largest stones from the heap, smash them together, and push the resulting weight back into the heap. We repeat this process until there is only one stone left in the heap, which will be the last stone weight. (We will slow down and draw it.)

solutions.python:
# Last Stone Weight
# Idea: To simulate the process of smashing stones, we can use a max-heap (priority queue) to keep track of the stone weights. At each step, we pop the two largest stones from the heap, smash them together, and push the resultin…
# Line comments below keep the same logic as the NeetCode 150 repo solution.

import heapq


class Solution:
    def lastStoneWeight(self, stones: List[int]) -> int:
        max_heap = [-stone for stone in stones]  # Use negative values for max-heap

        # Heap ops keep min/max ready

        heapq.heapify(max_heap)

        while len(max_heap) > 1:
            x = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)  # Extract the largest stone
            y = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)  # Extract the second largest stone

            if x != y:
                heapq.heappush(max_heap, -(x - y))  # Push the remaining weight

        return -max_heap[0] if max_heap else 0
